es: Sintetizar la información de un audio y de un texto: comparar lo que coincide, señalar las discrepancias y cerrar con una conclusión.

teaching.en: According to the radio report, the library closes in June, whereas the newspaper claims that it closes in July.
teaching.es: Según el informe de la radio, la biblioteca cierra en junio, mientras que el periódico afirma que cierra en julio.
teaching.explanationEs: Whereas contrasta dos fuentes: cada una con su dato, en una sola frase.
segments: According to the radio report, the library closes in June,
whereas the newspaper claims that it closes in July.
teaching.audioText: According to the radio report, the library closes in June, whereas the newspaper claims that it closes in July.

teaching.en: Both sources report a fall in visits, and likewise both attribute it to the new opening hours.
teaching.es: Las dos fuentes informan de una caída de visitas y, del mismo modo, ambas la atribuyen al nuevo horario.
teaching.explanationEs: Both + fuentes en plural + verbo sin -s. Likewise añade otra coincidencia.
segments: Both sources report a fall in visits, and likewise
both attribute it to the new opening hours.
teaching.audioText: Both sources report a fall in visits, and likewise both attribute it to the new opening hours.

teaching.en: The radio figure does not tally with the newspaper's, so a careful listener will cross-check both against the official record.
teaching.es: La cifra de la radio no coincide con la del periódico, así que un oyente cuidadoso contrastará las dos con el registro oficial.
teaching.explanationEs: Tally with = coincidir. Cross-check = contrastar con una segunda fuente. Figure = cifra.
segments: The radio figure does not tally with the newspaper's, so
a careful listener will cross-check both against the official record.
teaching.audioText: The radio figure does not tally with the newspaper's, so a careful listener will cross-check both against the official record.

teaching.en: When two conflicting accounts give different dates, name the discrepancy first and only then try to reconcile it.
teaching.es: Cuando dos versiones contradictorias dan fechas distintas, nombra la discrepancia primero y solo entonces intenta conciliarlas.
teaching.explanationEs: Discrepancy = diferencia entre datos. Reconcile = mostrar que dos datos pueden ser compatibles.
segments: When two conflicting accounts give different dates, name the
discrepancy first and only then try to reconcile it.
teaching.audioText: When two conflicting accounts give different dates, name the discrepancy first and only then try to reconcile it.

teaching.en: Judge each source by asking who is speaking, what they know and whether they gain from your believing them.
teaching.es: Juzga cada fuente preguntándote quién habla, qué sabe y si gana algo con que tú le creas.
teaching.explanationEs: Evaluar la fuente: quién habla, qué sabe y qué interés tiene. Es parte de una buena síntesis.
segments: Judge each source by asking who is speaking, what they
know and whether they gain from your believing them.
teaching.audioText: Judge each source by asking who is speaking, what they know and whether they gain from your believing them.

teaching.en: Taken together, the two sources agree on the problem, and overall the discrepancy concerns only the date.
teaching.es: En conjunto, las dos fuentes coinciden en el problema y, globalmente, la discrepancia afecta solo a la fecha.
teaching.explanationEs: Taken together y overall abren la conclusión: resumen coincidencias y diferencias en una frase.
segments: Taken together, the two sources agree on the problem,
and overall the discrepancy concerns only the date.
teaching.audioText: Taken together, the two sources agree on the problem, and overall the discrepancy concerns only the date.

prompt.es: Escucha la radio, lee el aviso y elige en qué discrepan las dos fuentes.

choices.text: The cost of the playground.
Whether the playground will be built at all.
The month in which the playground will open.

feedback.es: La radio dice mayo y el aviso del municipio dice junio: esa es la discrepancia. El aviso no da cifra, así que no contradice el coste, y las dos fuentes suponen que el parque se construirá.

hint.es: Compara el mes que da cada fuente.

origin.audio: The mayor says the new playground will open in May, and that it will cost two hundred thousand pounds.
origin.text: Council notice: The new playground will open in June. The final cost will be confirmed when the building work is complete.

prompt.es: Completa: «La radio dice cuatrocientos, mientras que el periódico da trescientos.»

feedback.es: Whereas une en una sola frase dos datos que se contrastan; while también es posible con este sentido.

hint.es: Es el conector que contrasta dos fuentes en una frase.

origin.text: The radio report says that four hundred people attended the march, ___ the newspaper gives three hundred. Nobody explains the difference.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En conjunto, ambas fuentes coinciden en el problema.»

answer.text: Overall both sources agree on the problem

feedback.es: Overall abre la conclusión; both sources lleva verbo en plural sin -s (agree).

hint.es: La conclusión empieza con el conector que resume.

prompt.es: ¿Qué valoración de las dos fuentes es la más acertada?

choices.text: B is better supported, but its figure is still an estimate.
A is more reliable because the owner was present.
Neither can be used because the two sources disagree.

feedback.es: La estimación apoyada en fotos es más sólida que un recuerdo impreciso, pero sigue siendo una estimación. Estar presente no garantiza exactitud, y una discrepancia no anula todas las fuentes.

origin.text: Source A: a shop owner says that hundreds of people joined the march. Source B: the police estimate, based on photographs taken from above, is three thousand.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con la función que cumple en una síntesis.

pairs.es: Contrasta dos datos en una sola frase
Añade otra coincidencia entre las fuentes
Coincidir con el dato de otra fuente
Resume lo que aportan las dos fuentes

feedback.es: Cada expresión cumple una función distinta: contrastar, sumar coincidencias, comprobar y resumir.

pairs.es: Contrasta dos datos en una sola frase
Añade otra coincidencia entre las fuentes
Coincidir con el dato de otra fuente
Resume lo que aportan las dos fuentes

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo se relacionan las dos fuentes.

choices.text: They disagree about the size of the fall, and only one gives a cause.
They agree more or less on the size of the fall, but neither gives a cause.
They agree on the cause of the fall, although the figures are quite different from each other.

feedback.es: Un quinto y el dieciocho por ciento son cifras parecidas, y ninguna fuente explica el motivo. Las otras opciones inventan un desacuerdo o una causa.

origin.audio: The report on the radio says that visits to the library fell last year by about a fifth. The figure in the newspaper article is similar: it speaks of a drop of eighteen per cent. Neither source explains why the fall happened.

prompt.es: Escucha la radio, lee la noticia y elige qué se puede concluir de las dos versiones.

choices.text: They agree on the numbers of users, but differ on the dates of the closure.
They agree on everything except who will be responsible for the repairs.
They agree that the pool will close, but differ on dates and numbers.

feedback.es: Ambas hablan del cierre por reparaciones; la radio da junio-septiembre y unos cuatrocientos socios, y el periódico julio-octubre y unos trescientos: difieren en fechas y en cifras. No se habla de quién paga.

origin.audio: A local radio station reported this morning that the swimming pool will close for repairs in June and reopen in September. The manager told the station that about four hundred members use the pool every week, and that most of them are older people who have no other place to exercise.
origin.text: Town Gazette: The swimming pool will close from July for essential repairs, the council has confirmed. Around three hundred people use it each week, according to council records, and the work is expected to last until October.

prompt.es: ¿Qué podría explicar que la cifra de la radio sea mayor?

choices.text: The radio figure includes visitors who do not pay.
The manager has overstated the number of users to help his case.
The newspaper has mixed up its records of members and visitors.

feedback.es: El gerente cuenta a todos los que entran y el registro solo las entradas de pago: esa diferencia de método explica la discrepancia sin acusar a nadie. No hay pruebas de mala fe ni de que el periódico confundiera sus registros.

origin.text: The radio figure comes from the pool manager, who counts every member at the door. The newspaper figure comes from council records, which count only paid entries.

prompt.es: Completa: «Las dos estimaciones no coinciden entre sí.»

feedback.es: Tally with es la colocación habitual para cifras que cuadran; agree with o match with también son naturales.

origin.text: One report says four hundred people use the pool each week, and another says three hundred. The two estimates simply do not ___ with each other.

prompt.es: Escucha, lee y escribe una síntesis que compare la fecha y el número de pasajeros.

answer.text: According to the radio, the night bus will stop in March, whereas the newspaper says that it will be cut from April. Both sources agree that the company is ending the service, but they differ on the number of passengers: about thirty, according to the company, against nearly eighty, according to the campaign group. Overall, the discrepancy over the date and the figures suggests that the two sides are using different data.
accepted: According to the radio, the night bus will stop in March, whereas the newspaper says that it will be cut from April. Both sources agree that the company is ending the service, but they differ on the number of passengers: about thirty, according to the company, against nearly eighty, according to the campaign group. Overall, the discrepancy over the date and the figures suggests that the two sides are using different data.

The radio says the night bus will stop running in March, but the article gives April. The two sources agree that the service is ending, while they disagree about how many people use it: thirty, according to the company, and eighty, according to the campaign group. Taken together, the sources show a real discrepancy, and the figures may come from different counts.

feedback.es: Una buena síntesis compara en un párrafo: fecha de cada fuente, lo que coincide, cifras en contraste y una conclusión con overall o taken together.

origin.text: Article. Evening Post: The night bus on route twelve will be cut from April, the company has confirmed. A campaign group says that nearly eighty people use it every night, mostly hospital staff, and they have collected two thousand signatures.
origin.audio: The transport company announced today that the night bus on route twelve will stop running from March, because only about thirty passengers use it each night. A spokesperson added that a taxi service may replace it.

prompt.es: Escucha la radio, lee el texto y elige cómo se relacionan las dos fuentes.

choices.text: The text confirms the radio figure and shows that it applies to all workers.
The text supports the radio figure but limits how far it applies.
The text adds a cause that the radio did not mention.

feedback.es: El 21 por ciento coincide con «uno de cada cinco», y la advertencia sobre la muestra limita su alcance. El texto no generaliza a todos los trabajadores ni menciona una causa.

origin.audio: Researchers told a radio show that about one in five commuters now works from home at least three days a week.
origin.text: Transport Weekly: A new survey of two thousand commuters finds that twenty-one per cent work from home at least three days a week, although the authors warn that the sample came mainly from city offices.

prompt.es: ¿Qué concluye la autora sobre las dos noticias?

choices.text: That the sources do not really conflict, because they refer to different events.
That one source is clearly more reliable than the other, and should be trusted.
That the date is unknown, so the reports cannot be compared.
That both sources made a mistake in reporting the date.

feedback.es: «Smaller than it looks» significa que la discrepancia es solo aparente: hablan de hechos distintos. No declara una fuente más fiable ni imposible la comparación.

origin.text: The two reports differ on the date, but a closer look shows that the radio gave the start of the works, whereas the newspaper gave the date of the official opening. The discrepancy is therefore smaller than it looks.

prompt.es: Completa: «Del mismo modo, el periódico lo describió como una clara mejora.»

feedback.es: Likewise añade una coincidencia entre las fuentes; Similarly tiene el mismo sentido en este contexto.

origin.text: The radio report praised the new timetable for its reliability. ___, the newspaper described it as a clear improvement on the old one.
